//: Recommended Visual Studio Code extensions for DungeonLike.
This list covers languages Visual Studio Code cannot colour on its own, and
nothing else. It deliberately recommends no build, test, lint, debug or
workflow tooling, because the repository's verification policy states that
Gradle tasks, builds, tests, Android tooling, emulators and packaging are
never run locally -- all executable verification happens in GitHub Actions
(AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md). An extension that exists to build or test the
project locally would recommend a workflow the project does not permit.
SELECTION BAR: each entry is either published by a Marketplace publisher
whose domain is verified, or maintained in the language's own upstream
project. Verification status is stated per entry rather than implied, so a
reader can judge the trust decision instead of taking it on faith.

geequlim.godot-tools: GDScript, scene and resource syntax highlighting: .gd, .tscn, .tres,
.godot, .import and .gdshader -- none of which Visual Studio Code knows.
The game core is written in this language, so without it the largest body
of code in the repository is plain grey text.
PROVENANCE: the Marketplace publisher 'Geequlim' is NOT domain-verified.
The extension is nevertheless the official one: it is developed in the
Godot organisation's own repository, godotengine/godot-vscode-plugin, and
no alternative with a verified publisher exists. Stated plainly here
rather than omitted, because an unverified publisher is a real, if small,
supply-chain consideration and the reader should get to weigh it.
JetBrains.kotlin-server: Kotlin syntax highlighting for the Android host module.
and the vendor of the language itself.
KNOWN GAP: this extension registers the .kt extension only, so Gradle
Kotlin DSL files (build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle.kts) are not
highlighted by default. .vscode/settings.json maps *.kts to the Kotlin
language to close that gap without recommending a second extension.
